claims.text: The quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys have identical thermomechanical processing histories.
All compared alloys are single-phase FCC.
All compared alloys have homogeneous chemical compositions.
High-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction can quantify the relevant local lattice strains.
In situ neutron diffraction during mechanical testing can quantify the relevant dislocation dynamics.
Adding the fifth element to the quinary alloy produces larger local lattice distortions than occur in the corresponding quaternary and ternary subsets.
Atomic-size misfit associated with the fifth element broadens the distribution of local lattice strains in the quinary alloy.
Greater local-strain heterogeneity impedes dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases the quinary alloy's yield strength relative to the quaternary and ternary subsets.
Impeded dislocation motion increases the quinary alloy's work-hardening rate relative to the quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quaternary and ternary subsets have less extensive local lattice distortion than the quinary alloy.
The quaternary and ternary subsets exhibit lower mechanical resistance than the quinary alloy.
The predicted trends are limited to single-phase FCC alloys with identical processing histories tested at room temperature and controlled strain rates.
